significance: A 17th-century pagoda temple on the Punyamata river a kilometre from Banepa, carrying carved struts and a vast painted Bhairava said to be the largest wall painting in the Nepal Mandala. Its outer wall bears a mural of the goddess killing the demon Chanda.
story: The goddess is said to have destroyed the demon Chanda, whom Shiva's boon had made invulnerable to all but a woman, after he felled the tree she hid in; a lingam grew from his body and stands in a small shrine nearby.
